title: Affirm, other BNPL players ratchet up credit bureau reporting
summary: Trade-press article reports that Affirm and other BNPL firms are beginning to report loan data to credit bureaus and what that means for scoring.

assertions.quote: Affirm will begin reporting all BNPL transactions to the credit bureau Experian beginning April 1
if I took out 10 of those this year, that's a really big risk signal that there's something wrong with my cash flows and my ability

verdicts.note: Matches credit-bureau analysts' own description of heavy unsecured-installment-loan use as a risk signal in underwriting.

FICO's year-long joint study found a 'unique consumer behavior' of BNPL borrowers opening a large number of loans within a short period, significant enough that FICO built a new scoring treatment (aggregating separate BNPL loans together) specifically to handle it rather than let each one register as a standard new-account event.
CFPB frames 'loan stacking' -- taking out several BNPL loans within a short time frame at simultaneous lenders -- as one of its two core overextension risks.

assertions.quote: many BNPL users are younger and skew toward the lower end of the credit spectrum
